haiku-low.q1: They get the generic 200 reply, 'If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link.' Nothing is sent: no row and no job.
haiku-low.q2: Its 4th request is rolled back: no reset_sends row, no new token, no email queued. It gets the same generic reply, and the existing link stays valid.
haiku-low.q3: 30 minutes from issue. It ends sooner when the link is used, or when a newer link is issued, since the worker's upsert replaces the old token.
haiku-low.q4: Still unused and valid until it expires. The form is shown again with an error, so the user can retry.
haiku-low.q5: None. All sessions rows for the user are deleted, including this device, and other devices are logged out on their next request. No cookie is set, so the user logs in again at /login.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job. Nobody is told, though the user was told a link was sent.
haiku-low.q7: The worker generates the 32-byte token and emails it inside the link https://<app>/reset?t=<token>. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored.
haiku-low.q8: The server hashes the token with SHA-256 and finds the row with that token_hash where used_at is empty and expires_at is later than now. No row means the expired page.
haiku-low.q9: In the reset_sends table, one row per send (user_id, sent_at), counted over the last hour. Rows older than 1 hour are purged.
haiku-low.q10: The worker's upsert overwrites the account's single password_reset_tokens row, killing the old link. This happens when the worker makes the new token, not at request time.
haiku-low.q11: Together in one transaction, before COMMIT: used_at set, password_hash updated, sessions deleted, 'password changed' job added (if queue is Postgres-backed).
haiku-low.q12: One atomic UPDATE sets used_at only where the hash matches and the link is unused and unexpired. Only one submission changes a row; the other gets 0 rows, rolls back, and sees the expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see the same generic 200 reply ("If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link.") with the same minimum response time. Nothing is sent; no row and no job.
sonnet.q2: The fourth request (3 or more sends in the last hour) is rolled back: no reset_sends row, no new token, no email queued. The user gets the same generic 200 reply, and nobody is told. Any existing link stays valid.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes from when the worker creates the token. It can end sooner by being used (used_at set), or by a newer link being issued, since the worker's upsert overwrites the old token hash.
sonnet.q4: Unchanged: still unused and valid. The form is shown again with an error, and the user can retry until the link expires.
sonnet.q5: None. All the user's sessions rows are deleted (all devices, including the one that made the request). No session cookie is set. The user is redirected (303) to /login and logs in again by hand with the new password.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job. The user is not told. They were already told a link was sent. The design suggests alerting on dropped jobs and a support runbook. The user can request again, which uses one send slot.
sonnet.q7: The API does not make the token. It records a reset_sends row and queues a job with only user_id and send_id. The email worker generates the 32 random byte token, stores only its SHA-256 hash, and puts the raw token directly into the emailed link (https://<app>/reset?t=<token>).
sonnet.q8: The API hashes the token from the URL with SHA-256 and looks for a password_reset_tokens row where token_hash matches the hash, used_at is empty and expires_at is later than now. If found, the form is shown; if not, the expired page.
sonnet.q9: In the reset_sends table (one row per request, with sent_at, indexed on (user_id, sent_at)). The count is of rows from the last hour. Old rows drop out by being purged when older than 1 hour.
sonnet.q10: The earlier link is killed by overwriting (upsert) the account's single password_reset_tokens row with the new hash, expiry and used_at cleared. This happens when the email worker makes the new token, not when the request is made. That is normally seconds, but longer if the queue is backed up.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: the atomic UPDATE marking the link used, the new argon2id password hash stored in users.password_hash, and deletion of all the user's sessions rows. The "password changed" email is added as an outbox job in that same transaction, before COMMIT. Whether it truly commits together depends on the queue being Postgres-backed, which is an open question.
sonnet.q12: Through the single atomic UPDATE inside the transaction. It sets used_at only where the hash matches and the link is still unused and unexpired. Only one submission changes a row. The second changes 0 rows, rolls back, and gets the expired page.
